applies_to: WaterFurnace single-compressor water-to-air console heat pumps fitted with the FX10 DDC controller.
summary: BACnet objects for WaterFurnace's single-compressor console heat pump on the FX10 controller. It is a short list: space and discharge air temperatures, effective setpoints, an alarm code, flash-stored setpoints and limits, and read-only status of the fan, compressor, reversing valve and two digital inputs. The BAS can shift both setpoints with Space Setpoint (AO1) and override the space temperature (AO2).
notes: Output-type points (AO/MO) are volatile and fall back to uncommanded after a power cycle; unlimited writes.
Value-type points (AV/MV) are stored in flash (about 2,000,000 write life); never write them from automatic reset logic.
Multistate numbers assume the BAS shows 255 as uncommanded; if yours shows 254, every state number is one lower (0=Off, 1=On).
Units are not printed on the sheet. The sheet does not state the BACnet transport.
This sheet has no occupancy command, fan/compressor command or alarm reset point.
Alarm codes 5-7 are not listed in the alarm table.

source.title: BACnet Points for Single Compressor Water-to-Air Console Units Utilizing the FX10 Controller

integration.summary: The console unit runs on its own setpoints; the BAS mainly adjusts them and monitors. Use Space Setpoint (AO1) to move both setpoints from one command, or AO2 to feed a network space temperature. Keep frequent writes on the volatile AO points, not the flash-backed AV setpoints.

minimum_points.name: Space Setpoint
minimum_points.why: Midpoint setpoint; shifts heat and cool together

integration.enable: The sheet has no enable, occupancy or shutdown command; the unit runs on its local control and the BAS adjusts setpoints.
integration.remote_sensors: AO2 Space Temp Override replaces the space sensor reading from the network. It is a volatile output, so it reverts to uncommanded after a power cycle.
gotchas: AV points are stored in flash (about 2,000,000 writes); write them only manually or by schedule, never from automatic reset logic.
Output points (AO) are volatile and go back to uncommanded after a power cycle, so rewrite them after power returns.
If the BAS shows 254 as uncommanded instead of 255, every multistate value is one lower.
